text:
olivia (CS): Hey team — customer A reported a sudden increase in 429s and what looks like duplicate processing/charges after they upgraded to SDK v2.x. They do batched embeddings with ~50 concurrent workers. No idempotency keys in their current integration. Seeing lots of `Retry-After` followed by immediate retries from the client and then success. Can eng-infra help triage?

jake (eng-infra): thanks olivia. do we have request/response samples and whether these are streaming or non-streaming calls? also any x-ratelimit-* headers captured?

olivia (CS): attached snippet from their logs (redacted):
```
HTTP 429 
x-ratelimit-limit: 600
x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-ratelimit-reset: 1670000
Retry-After: 3

client: got 429, retrying immediately (sdk retry count 4)
client: success on retry
```
They say SDK defaults changed in 2.x but aren't sure which setting. They also pasted their SDK init: 
```
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., retry_policy="default", concurrency=50)
```
No idempotency token anywhere.

maria (eng-runtime): quick thought — if a lot of clients are concurrently hitting remaining=0 then many will see Retry-After and attempt retries in the same short window. SDK defaults matter: if default uses exponential backoff with low base and high max retries + jitter that can still cluster. also embedding endpoints are rate-limited per-project per-minute in a token-bucket way; bursts after a reset will cause sustained token drain.

jake (eng-infra): can you ask customer for exact SDK version and whether they were on v1.x before? also ask for a small repro script (we can run internally) showing concurrency and the exact retry settings.

olivia (CS): customer said: upgraded from 1.9.2 -> 2.0.1 last week. They ran a quick repro loop for us: 
```
# simplified repro
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(key="XXX", retry_policy="default")
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

def call():
    client.embeddings.create(input=["a"]*16)

with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=50) as ex:
    for _ in range(200):
        ex.submit(call)
```
They said 429s spike then many requests succeed after retrying, but they see duplicate downstream processing because they re-process on every success (they don't check idempotency).

maria (eng-runtime): OK — two pieces of guidance: 1) strongly recommend idempotency keys for non-read operations (or any operation where duplicate processing is problematic). For embeddings specifically, results are deterministic for same input+model, but their pipeline re-ingests results and triggers billing downstream. 2) For SDK config: limit concurrency, set conservative retry policy and add jitter. Example suggestion to customer: 
```
client = RedwoodClient(
  key="XXX",
  retry_policy={
    "max_retries": 3,
    "backoff": "exponential",
    "base_delay_ms": 500,
    "max_delay_ms": 5000,
    "jitter": true
  },
  concurrency_limit=10
)
# add idempotency token per logical request
client.headers.update({"Idempotency-Key": generate_uuid()})
```
That should spread retries and avoid big retry storms.

jake (eng-infra): also check for SDK behavior change between 1.x and 2.x: I think v2 switched default base_delay from 250ms -> 100ms and increased max_retries from 3 -> 5 in some profiles. that would make retries more aggressive. we should confirm and patch docs/consider a 'safety' preset.

olivia (CS): customer asked if server-side rate-limit headers can be used to coordinate backoff across workers (they have many short-lived processes). any recommended header handling?

maria (eng-runtime): yes — honor Retry-After and implement global backoff per API key: when Retry-After observed, throttle new outbound calls for that key for that duration (or until x-ratelimit-remaining > 0). For ephemeral processes, use a small central coordinator or cache (redis) to store backoff-until timestamp. Also prefer linear or capped exponential backoff for secondaries to avoid burst convergence.

jake (eng-infra): for our side, we should make x-ratelimit-* visible in logs and in the console per-route. devex: can we add a short KB about "Coordinator patterns for Retry-After (ephemeral workers)"?

infra-bot: deploy 2630001200: added console metric for x-ratelimit header visibility on embeddings in staging.

olivia (CS): customer tried maria's suggested config and set concurrency to 8 + idempotency per logical job. they report immediate drop in duplicate downstream events and far fewer 429s after a day. they asked if Redwood has a recommended SDK preset for "high-concurrency burst-safe" — we should propose one.

maria (eng-runtime): propose adding a preset `retry_profile: "burst-safe"` that sets base_delay_ms=400, max_retries=3, jitter=true, concurrency_suggestion=10. file an eng task ticket for adding preset + doc.

jake (eng-infra): noted. i'll follow up on the SDK changelog callout about v2 defaults. we should also add a short support playbook for customers who see this pattern: 1) capture x-ratelimit headers, 2) reduce concurrency, 3) use idempotency, 4) use global Retry-After coordination, 5) enable burst-safe preset.

olivia (CS): thanks all — closing the SLA ticket after customer confirmed mitigation. saved repro snippet and our recommended config in the ticket. :thumbsup:
